We need to analyze candidate.py for correctness relative to SPEC.md: unique_by(items, key) must return a new list with exactly one item for each distinct key(item), the first item in items having that key, placed in the order in which keys first appear. Do not modify items.

Candidate implementation: return list({key(item): item for item in items}.values())

This uses dict comprehension to map key(item) to item, then values() gives items in insertion order of keys (Python 3.7+). However, this will keep only last item for each key because dict will overwrite earlier entries. Also ordering may be the order of last occurrences, not first. For example, items [3,1,3,2,1] keys identity. dict comprehension will iterate over items: key=3, store {3:3}. Next key=1 store {3:3,1:1}. Next key=3 overwrite {3:3}? Actually key=3 again, will set {3:3} again same value. Then 2 -> {3:3,1:1,2:2}. Then 1 again will overwrite {1:1} again same value. The resulting values order is 3,1,2 which matches expected? In this case fine. But for different key function that maps multiple items to same key but different values, the dict will keep last item but spec wants first item. For example items=[1,2,3], key=lambda x: x%2. For 1 key 1, 2 key 0, 3 key 1. Desired output: [1,2] because key 1 first appears with 1. Candidate dict would have key 1 mapping to 3 (last), key 0 mapping to 2. Values order: 3,2 -> wrong.

Also if key function not unique per item but multiple items share key, first one is required. So candidate fails.

Also candidate does not preserve order when items have same key but different values, and might change order for keys that appear multiple times.

Also candidate modifies nothing to items. That is fine.

Thus a defect.
